title: Node.js has released security updates '22.23.4', '24.22.1', and '26.12.1', fixing a total of 10 vulnerabilities.
text:
Node.js has released security updates '22.23.4', '24.22.1', and '26.12.1', fixing a total of 10 vulnerabilities. - GIGAZINE 
 GIGAZINE 
 Twitter 
 Facebook

 Oct 22, 2026 16:30:00 
 Node.js has released security updates '22.23.4', '24.22.1', and '26.12.1', fixing a total of 10 vulnerabilities.
 The open-source JavaScript runtime environment 
 Node.js has received a security update that addresses 10 vulnerabilities. This update was released as scheduled, and the severity of the vulnerabilities fixed is as follows: 4 are 'high,' 3 are 'medium,' and 3 are 'low.'
 Node.js — Wednesday, October 21, 2026 Security Releases 
 https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases 
 🔐 Node.js security updates are now available!
 New releases for Node.js 22.x, 24.x & 26.x address multiple vulnerabilities, including high-severity issues.
 Review the details and update your systems to stay secure.
 🔗 https://t.co/W4kfzx5lxz
 #NodeJS #Security
 — Node.js (@nodejs) October 21, 2026 
 The fixed vulnerabilities include the following 10 issues, including 'CVE-2026-111497,' which allows the Node.js Brotli decoder to allow out-of-bounds writes, leading to remote code execution.
・4 cases with “high” severity level
 CVE-2026-105482 : Vulnerability in dns.resolve where names containing NUL characters are truncated.
 CVE-2026-105483 : Vulnerability that allows TLS certificate hostname verification to be bypassed by using an IP address written with full-width numerals.
 CVE-2026-106069 : Vulnerability that allows TLS certificate hostname verification to be bypassed by a hostname interpreted as an IP address.
 CVE-2026-111497 : Vulnerability that allows remote code execution through out-of-bounds writes to the Brotli decoder.
・3 cases with “medium” severity
 CVE-2026-105481 : Vulnerability in Keep-alive connections where responses written before a request is sent are processed.
 CVE-2026-106072 : A vulnerability exists where certificate validation for non-standard IPv4 addresses is inadequate, allowing authentication of IP address destinations via SANs for DNS names.
 CVE-2026-106074 : A vulnerability where the entropy cache of crypto.randomUUID() and randomInt() is stored in a startup snapshot or SEA, resulting in the same value being generated across multiple processes.
・3 cases of “low” severity
 CVE-2026-106070 : A vulnerability in Node.js's ZipFile that allows an attacker to control the leading byte sequence even after the ZIP header validation fails.
 CVE-2026-106071 : Vulnerability that allows excessive file system permissions to be granted through cardinal lookup using wildcards in the Permission Model.
 CVE-2026-106073 : Vulnerability that allows bypassing Permission Model access restrictions using fs.realpathSync.
 Of the 10 vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-105483, rated as 'high,' affects only Node.js 26.x and 24.x; CVE-2026-106070 and CVE-2026-106071, rated as 'low,' affect only Node.js 26.x; and the other 7 vulnerabilities are common to 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
